transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess the main reason is that I'm really scared of how I get when I start eating. Like, once I start, it doesn’t feel like I’m fully there anymore. It’s hard to explain, but it’s like I sort of disappear in my own head and something else takes over, and I’m watching it happen but I can’t actually stop it.

Even while it’s happening, I’m telling myself, “Stop, just stop now, you don’t have to keep going,” and I really mean it, but I keep eating anyway. It goes on until I feel like I can’t stand it anymore. It’s not just being hungry or liking food or whatever. It feels out of my control, and that’s why I came in.
Do you usually do anything to try to get rid of the food after one of these episodes where you feel like you're eating out of control?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I usually try to get somewhere private pretty quickly after, because once I realize what I’ve eaten, I get this horrible panic feeling, like the food is just sitting inside me and it’s going to turn into weight if I don’t do something right away.

So I’ll end up in a bathroom, usually in the dorm if I can get there, or sometimes I’ve gone to a quiet floor of the library where there aren’t many people around. And I make myself throw up. I don’t really like saying that out loud, but that’s what happens. It feels awful and embarrassing, but in the moment it feels like the only way to undo it or stop freaking out.
How often do these episodes of eating out of control happen?

It’s… it’s been a lot. Like, not every single day, but definitely several times a week. And it’s not just something that happened once or twice and then went away.

For most of this semester it’s been like this — the eating out of control and then throwing up after. I keep trying to tell myself, “Okay, this week I’m not going to do that,” but then a few days go by and it happens again. When I look back over the last few months, I honestly can’t really think of a full week where it completely stopped. It’s been pretty constant in that way, even if the exact number changes week to week.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, I know that sounds weird because I think about my body and weight a lot, but I don’t have a clear number to give you.

I don’t weigh myself in a super consistent way, and when I do it kind of depends on the time of day or what I’ve eaten or whether I’m already upset, so I don’t know how reliable it is. Sometimes I’ll feel like I look different from one day to the next, but then I also know that might just be in my head, or because I’m bloated or whatever.

So… significant changes? I don’t know. I haven’t noticed anything really obvious like people commenting on it or my clothes suddenly not fitting, at least not in a way I can say for sure. I just don’t feel like I can answer that with a definite yes or no.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah. Very afraid. It’s kind of… it’s hard to explain without sounding ridiculous, but it doesn’t feel like just, “Oh, I’d rather not gain weight.” It feels like if I gain weight, or even if I just think I look bigger, everything about me kind of collapses in my head.

Like I can be having an okay day — I went to class, I talked to people, I didn’t mess anything up — and then I’ll walk past one of those dark dorm windows or a glass door and catch my reflection. If my stomach looks bigger, or my face looks rounder, especially compared to other guys walking near me, it’s like this instant drop in my chest. I’ll start thinking, “Everyone can see it. I look disgusting. I failed.” Even if nothing actually happened in the day, it suddenly feels like the whole day was ruined.

And then I don’t want anyone to look at me. I don’t want to go to the dining hall, or sit near people, or be seen from the side. It’s like my brain takes that one reflection and turns it into proof that something is wrong with me. So… yeah, I’m really scared of gaining weight. More than I want to admit.
Do you do anything else besides making yourself throw up to try to undo the effects of eating out of control?

I’m… not totally sure how to answer that, because I guess I don’t always think of it as a list of things I do, if that makes sense. The main thing I’m aware of is throwing up after. That’s the part that feels the most deliberate, like, “I need to get rid of this.”

Besides that, I don’t know. I mean, I’ll sometimes get in my head afterward and feel like I should do something to make up for it, but I’m not sure if you mean specific things. Like pills or something? I don’t really know. I don’t want to say no in a way that sounds too clean or certain, because when I’m upset after eating like that, my thoughts are all over the place and I’m just trying to stop feeling panicked.

But in terms of actual things I do to undo it… I think the throwing up is the main thing. I can’t really point to another clear thing the same way.
Do you exercise more than what's considered typical for someone of your age and health status?

I don’t really know. I mean, I don’t think so in the way you might mean, like some kind of intense workout routine or training for hours every day. I’m not on a team or anything, and I wouldn’t say I’m, like, a fitness person.

But I also don’t know what counts as “more than typical,” because compared to some people at school I probably don’t do that much, and compared to other people maybe I do more. Sometimes I’ll walk around campus a lot, or take longer routes, but I don’t know if that’s exercise-exercise or just me being restless and not wanting to sit still. It’s hard for me to separate those things.

I guess I wouldn’t say I have a clear pattern of exercising a lot to make up for eating, if that’s what you’re asking. Not the way the throwing up feels clear in my head. With exercise, I can’t point to something definite and say, “Yes, I’m doing way too much.” It’s more vague than that.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics after eating to try to undo the effects?

No… I mean, not laxatives or water pills or anything like that. I don’t really do that.

After I eat like that, the thing I usually end up doing is finding a bathroom somewhere — like in the dorm, or sometimes on a quiet floor of the library where I think no one’s really around — and making myself throw up. It’s like once I’ve eaten and I feel out of control, I can’t stop thinking that the food is just sitting inside me and turning into weight. I know that sounds… I don’t know, extreme, but that’s how it feels in the moment. Like I have to get it out before it becomes part of me.

So, no to laxatives or diuretics. It’s mostly vomiting.
